messages:
Amit: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a tiny SDK primitive called "session marker" to decouple resume semantics from opaque server tokens. sketch below and tradeoffs. want eyeballs before I open the RFC PR.

Neha: tl;dr? how is this different from existing resume token / lease ideas we've discussed?

Amit: TL;DR: current resume tokens are opaque and server-shaped. session marker = client-visible monotonic marker + ttl. Transport maps it to server token when supported. Benefits: predictable client semantics across Python/TS/Go, simpler retry reasoning, and easier streaming <> paged convergence.

Samira: curious: concrete example for streaming vs paged?

Amit: streaming: marker = last-consumed-seq (client). On reconnect transport asks server for messages with seq > marker. paged: marker maps to page cursor. If server doesn't support resume, transport returns not-resumable and SDK falls back to restart + dedupe heuristics.

Neha: so SDK synthesizes marker when server gives opaque token? or server would emit marker?

Amit: both supported. Preferred: server emits marker (more accurate). Fallback: SDK derives a best-effort marker (e.g., offset+hash) so clients still get consistent semantics.

Samira: how about retries and idempotency boundaries?

Amit: marker is read-only primitive — only for consumption. Writes keep existing idempotency keys. For concurrent readers, marker must be monotonic; servers should interpret ">= marker" resume queries. If server can't honour linearizability it returns not-resumable. SDK then triggers conservative fallback.

Neha: this is a new surface across languages. ergonomics concerns for Python/TS/Go?

Amit: proposal: expose a tiny value object: in Python a dataclass, TS an interface/class, Go a struct. Surface: marker.toString(), marker.ttl_ms, marker.monotonic (int) and optional signature. No methods that perform network effects. Simple equality and serialisation.

Samira: any perf impact? prefetch interplay?

Amit: default: ttl=30_000ms, prefetch_window=2 pages. SDK recommends small prefetch by default to keep markers fresh. We can make prefetch configurable per-client/route.

Neha: migration plan? breaking changes?

Amit: non-breaking for servers that keep emitting opaque tokens — transports can translate. Breaking only if we change existing resume token semantics; plan is additive. Migration doc + examples for python/ts/go in the RFC.

Samira: example snippet for transport mapping would help in the RFC. also tests: e2e resume + flaky network.

Amit: agreed. I'll add a prototype transport adapter and unit + e2e tests to the PR.

deploy-bot: deploy status — branch rfc/session-markers built and passed staging tests (identifier: build-1723). :white_check_mark:

Neha: +1 to RFC. can you include a short section on when servers should prefer server-side markers vs server tokens?

Amit: will do. Migration examples for python/ts/go and a minimal proto in the PR. opening RFC in ~1h.

Samira: awesome, thanks. :thumbsup:

Amit: pinging @Samira @Neha when RFC is up.
